scope: Targeted primary-source comparisons for the normalized weak-light limit, not an exhaustive novelty search

sources.title: Relay Feedback and Multivariable Control
sources.author: Karl Henrik Johansson
sources.access: Complete 179-page thesis downloaded and text-extracted; printed p.25, Example 15, visually checked
sources.comparison: Reproduces Cook's unstable second-order G=-1/(s^2-0.1s+1), with unit hysteresis. Different from stable third-order zero-hysteresis limiting slider.
sources.limit: Cook's original 1985 paper was not retrieved. This is a verified thesis reproduction, not a complete audit of Cook.

sources.title: On asymmetric periodic solutions in relay feedback systems
sources.access: Publisher-indexed abstract and section excerpts; direct open returned 403
sources.comparison: Atherton example W=1/[(s-d)(s^2+2s+10)], with the displayed regime described as two unstable saddle-focus equilibria. This is already the same broad factored third-order transfer family.
sources.limit: Complete article and cited Atherton reference not read; no claim to exclude matching parameter regimes elsewhere.

sources.title: Global Analysis of Third-Order Relay Feedback Systems
sources.access: University abstract read; linked report https://portal.research.lu.se/files/11036859/7542.pdf was not retrieved (web 403, Python expired-certificate error)
sources.limit: No inference that the abstract's global-convergence class includes all stable third-order biased relay systems.

sources.title: An Introduction to Nonlinearity in Control Systems
sources.author: Derek Atherton
sources.access: Complete 176-page book downloaded and text-extracted; pp.111-114 read, pp.112-113 visually checked
sources.comparison: Author's later account Section6.6.5 connects Amrani-Atherton1989 to cubic relay examples a0=4,a1=1.25,complex-unstable pair at a2<3.2; displayed chaos between2.8 and3.2.
sources.limit: Original 1989 proceedings paper not fully retrieved; other examples and general nonlinear equivalences remain unaudited.

conclusion: General relay chaos is established. Specific displayed examples differ, but neither first stable-relay chaos nor first physical elastomer chaos is claimed. Source PDFs remain local and are not redistributed under the repository MIT license.
